items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: T-Bone Walker come through with Les Hyte's big band ... oh, so many musicians.

ctx.x: But I stayed with that band from the summer of '39 up until the summer of '41 -- 6 months here, 4 months here, Quincy, Illinois; Springfield, Illinois; Grand Rapids, Michigan, and then back to Quincy. The last time I played Quincy with Flip, who comes in upstairs -- because the Casino Blue Room was a big rambling nightclub where they had the Blue Room downstairs and upstairs they had the big dancehall; they'd bring bands in there, and -- Kay Kaiser, his band with Ginny Simms -- all those kind of bands would come.

And I was just happy. And when we played Springfield, Illinois, this was during the period of the Springfield State Fair -- it was another state fair -- you used to see all kinds of bands out there. Some came out of St. Louis -- Louis Armstrong had a big band come through. T-Bone Walker come through with Les Hyte's big band ... oh, so many musicians. It
was jammed all day. Go all day and come back and jam all night. And then we went to Grand Rapids, Michigan -- but that's another story.
